source.title: New Gradient-Weighted Adaptive Gradient Methods With Dynamic Constraints
source.authors: Dong Liang; Fan-Fan Ma; Wenyan Li

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text is present. Some referenced tables are not reproduced in the supplied text, so their numerical values cannot be extracted.
record.tranche_reason: Compares adaptive optimizers with SGD and other adaptive methods on held-out performance, using different models, datasets, and optimizer variants from the claim’s cited studies.
record.gate_note: The paper reports optimizer comparisons bearing on V4. Its proposed GWDC and AMSGWDC are evaluated as methods; their results are included where they report test performance. Mentioned related-work findings are not extracted as rows.
record.test_reason: The study directly compares held-out performance of adaptive optimizers and SGD(M), bearing on V4 in MNIST, CIFAR-10 and character-level Penn Treebank settings. Its tuning differs from V4's strict learning-rate-and-schedule-only condition: Adam and AMSGrad also have beta parameters searched.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate as a statement of the authors' conclusion: they attribute improved convergence and generalization to dynamically increasing the weight of recent gradients in GWDC and AMSGWDC. They also conclude that AMSGrad offers little improvement over Adam and that learning-rate bounds improve their performance.
record.recipe_differences: Uses optimizer comparisons on MNIST, CIFAR-10 and character-level Penn Treebank with different architectures and added GWDC/AMSGWDC variants; reports five-seed averages for classification, but the supplied text omits the table values.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported optimizer ranking differs by model and task: SGD(M) beats Adam and AMSGrad in some MNIST/CIFAR-10 settings, while SGD is worse overall on the Penn Treebank GRU; the CIFAR-10 comparisons also describe performance after the learning-rate drop.

fits_no_version.finding: GWDC and AMSGWDC improve reported test performance or early progress over the selected comparators.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Dynamic weighting of recent gradients combined with bounded learning rates can improve optimization and held-out performance in these tested models.

record.problems: Numerical contents of Tables 3–5 are absent from the supplied text; most figure results are described qualitatively. The paper reports five random seeds for its experiments but does not provide the associated numerical uncertainty values in the supplied text.
record.rows_left_out: No separately described optimizer result was left out. Table entries are referenced but their numerical values are not present in the supplied text.

untested.parts: Convolutional versus fully connected architecture comparisons and local connectivity.

A strict learning-rate-and-schedule-only tuning protocol; systematic broader-tuning comparisons; decoupled weight decay; switching from Adam to SGD; word-level language modeling. Equal or better training performance is not established for every optimizer comparison.
Batch-size interventions and adapted large-batch recipes.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its relationship to generalization gaps.
Removing memorized versus randomly selected examples.

missing.what: AdaBound and AMSBound outperform SGD(M) on DenseNet-121 after the learning-rate reduction; add this comparator result separately from proposed-method gains.
On the two-hidden-layer MNIST network, SGD has higher accuracy than AdaBound and AMSBound, unlike the one-hidden-layer result.

For one-hidden-layer MNIST, nearly all optimizers except Adagrad reach approximately 100% training accuracy, while Adam and AMSGrad show severe test-loss overfitting. These results supply the training-performance context missing from R1.

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source for V4. Numerical table entries and plotted values are unavailable in the supplied text, so verdicts rely on explicit qualitative comparisons. Fixed architecture settings for dropout, weight decay and batch size do not test V5 or V6; comparing architectures on different datasets does not test V3.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and natural-label generalization are not evaluated.
No width sweep or interpolation-threshold analysis.

Tests selected adaptive and non-adaptive optimizers on MNIST, CIFAR-10 and Penn Treebank. Does not test language benchmarks beyond character-level Penn Treebank, broad hyperparameter tuning, decoupled weight decay, or switching from Adam to SGD.
No sharpness or other generalization-measure analysis.
No example removal or memorization-based selection.

statements.correction: Character-level Penn Treebank; three-layer GRU; 500 epochs; perplexity; SGD and Adagrad worse overall than the other optimizers; Adam and AMSGrad beta parameters searched; evidence of a setting-dependent optimizer ranking, not a demonstrated failure under V4's restricted tuning condition.
statements.problem: The character-level PTB setting, three-layer GRU, 500 epochs and qualitative ranking are supported. Calling this a challenge to V4 overstates the evidence: Adam and AMSGrad also have beta parameters searched, whereas V4's main comparison specifies learning-rate-and-schedule-only tuning and already allows reversals under broader tuning.
